goal: Force a declared risk of at least material whenever an intent's scope_hint touches kernel or authority paths, regardless of the tier the author wrote. Today the tier is planner self-graded and nothing cross-checks it against what the intent actually proposes to modify, so a routine declaration over kernel paths silently buys weaker gating precisely where gating matters most. The floor must be derived from scope_hint deterministically rather than from prose or from the author's judgment. This lands before or with any relocation of the enrollment confirmation, because every tier-based exemption downstream otherwise rests on self-grading; approving that exemption first and adding the floor later would leave a window in which a mis-tiered kernel change skips the gate. Relocating the confirmation itself and deleting the confirmation deadwood are separate slices and out of scope.

acceptance.assertion: An intent declaring routine with a scope_hint touching kernel or authority paths is rejected or promoted to at least material, and the outcome is derived from scope_hint rather than from any prose field.
An intent declaring routine with a scope_hint touching only documentation or ordinary test paths keeps its declared tier, so the floor does not silently escalate every task.
